risks.note: Operations in industrial engineering and industrial automation are exposed to working capital and liquidity risk arising from inventory requirements, project execution cycles and customer receivable periods. Any delay in collection of receivables, increase in inventory holding or change in project timelines may impact cash flows. Mitigated through cash flow planning, receivables monitoring, inventory optimisation and periodic review of funding requirements.

The Infra & Water segment operates across multiple states and requires coordination with various stakeholders. Risks include delays in civil readiness, obtaining municipal approvals and payment holds on the client side, which can cause cost overruns, accumulation of unbilled revenues and blockage of working capital. The Company is institutionalising dedicated project management teams, digital execution tracking and selective bidding guided by pre-defined risk filters.
risks.risk: Project execution and site readiness delays in the Infra & Water segment

risks.note: Rapid advances in automation solutions, digital technologies, control systems, AI-enabled analytics, IIoT, cloud-based monitoring, wireless instrumentation, smart sensors and self-calibrating technologies may accelerate product obsolescence. Failure to adopt emerging technologies or upgrade existing solutions may impact competitiveness, operational efficiency and market opportunities, and requires ongoing R&D spend.

The Company depends on the timely availability of specialised electronic components, sensors, analysers and imported equipment, and is exposed to raw material price fluctuations and extended lead times. Global supply chain disruptions, logistics challenges, geopolitical uncertainty or supplier constraints may affect production schedules, project execution timelines and cost efficiency.

The instrumentation and automation market is highly competitive with domestic and international players competing aggressively on price, which may compress margins particularly in commoditized product segments. Management explicitly flags that increasing imports from the Chinese market have intensified competition due to growing customer acceptance of Chinese products.
risks.risk: Price competition, including intensifying competition from Chinese imports

risks.note: Exposure to variations in regional economic conditions, regulatory requirements, project-specific factors and demand shifts across markets. Any slowdown in key markets, regional disruption or change in government policy may impact business opportunities, project execution and revenue growth. Mitigated by diversifying the customer base and spreading presence across sectors and geographies.
risks.risk: Geographical concentration and regional demand risk

risks.note: International expansion — now including subsidiaries in England, Germany and Saudi Arabia — requires compliance with diverse regulatory standards, certification requirements, trade policies and region-specific economic conditions, and exposes the Company to geopolitical developments and foreign exchange fluctuations that may impact project execution and profitability.

Availability and retention of skilled professionals in engineering, technical sales, project execution and after-sales support is critical to long-term success; competition for experienced talent from multinationals and industry peers may impact business continuity.

It incorporated three new wholly owned subsidiaries: Brix Engineering Limited in England (August 2025) to manufacture engineering products for industrial process automation and extend reach into Southeast Asia; Axis New Energy Private Limited / Axtevate Go Private Limited in India (April 2025) to build an EV ecosystem covering EV charging equipment manufacturing, integrated charging solutions and related technologies, with solar-based power generation also under exploration; and, subsequent to the year-end per the Corporate Governance Report, AxisSol Arabia Company in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia for oil & gas field machinery, installation of industrial machinery and installation of industrial process control equipment. On the existing base, the Company reports it continued strengthening its ATEX and IECEx-certified manufacturing facilities, adopted Lean Manufacturing across operations, enhanced its Calibration & Integration Laboratory, strengthened its DSIR-approved Research & Development Centre, and expanded capability into Marine, Offshore, Defence, Railways, Nuclear, Renewable Energy and Data Centers. On the utilities side it commissioned a 160 kW On-Grid Solar Power Plant at one of its manufacturing facilities and installed EV charging infrastructure at its premises. It also established a Centre of Excellence for Instrumentation with Government Engineering College, Gandhinagar. No rupee capex quantum, project cost, plant location list or commissioning timetable is disclosed anywhere in this bundle.

risks.note: Operations in industrial engineering and industrial automation are exposed to working capital and liquidity risk arising from inventory requirements, project execution cycles and customer receivable periods. Any delay in collection of receivables, increase in inventory holding or change in project timelines may impact cash flows. Mitigated through cash flow planning, receivables monitoring, inventory optimisation and periodic review of funding requirements.

risks.risk: Project execution and site readiness delays in the Infra & Water segment
risks.note: The Infra & Water segment operates across multiple states and requires coordination with various stakeholders. Risks include delays in civil readiness, obtaining municipal approvals and payment holds on the client side, which can cause cost overruns, accumulation of unbilled revenues and blockage of working capital. The Company is institutionalising dedicated project management teams, digital execution tracking and selective bidding guided by pre-defined risk filters.

Rapid advances in automation solutions, digital technologies, control systems, AI-enabled analytics, IIoT, cloud-based monitoring, wireless instrumentation, smart sensors and self-calibrating technologies may accelerate product obsolescence. Failure to adopt emerging technologies or upgrade existing solutions may impact competitiveness, operational efficiency and market opportunities, and requires ongoing R&D spend.

The Company depends on the timely availability of specialised electronic components, sensors, analysers and imported equipment, and is exposed to raw material price fluctuations and extended lead times. Global supply chain disruptions, logistics challenges, geopolitical uncertainty or supplier constraints may affect production schedules, project execution timelines and cost efficiency.

risks.risk: Price competition, including intensifying competition from Chinese imports
risks.note: The instrumentation and automation market is highly competitive with domestic and international players competing aggressively on price, which may compress margins particularly in commoditized product segments. Management explicitly flags that increasing imports from the Chinese market have intensified competition due to growing customer acceptance of Chinese products.

risks.risk: Geographical concentration and regional demand risk
risks.note: Exposure to variations in regional economic conditions, regulatory requirements, project-specific factors and demand shifts across markets. Any slowdown in key markets, regional disruption or change in government policy may impact business opportunities, project execution and revenue growth. Mitigated by diversifying the customer base and spreading presence across sectors and geographies.

International expansion — now including subsidiaries in England, Germany and Saudi Arabia — requires compliance with diverse regulatory standards, certification requirements, trade policies and region-specific economic conditions, and exposes the Company to geopolitical developments and foreign exchange fluctuations that may impact project execution and profitability.

Availability and retention of skilled professionals in engineering, technical sales, project execution and after-sales support is critical to long-term success; competition for experienced talent from multinationals and industry peers may impact business continuity.

As industrial operations adopt connected devices, cloud platforms and remote monitoring, cyber threats, data security risks and evolving customer cybersecurity requirements necessitate continuous investment in secure digital infrastructure to maintain customer confidence and business continuity.
